newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Consumer prices 0.3 percent in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Consumer prices 0.3 percent in December.

text.p: Consumer prices in December edged higher as inflation for all of 1996 rose at the fastest rate in six years, the Labor Department said Tuesday.
The Department said the consumer price index rose 0.3 percent in December, identical with November's rise.
However, with the often-volatile food and energy sector removed, the so-called core rate increased more modestly, rising only 0.1 percent after being up 0.2 percent in November.
For all of 1996, consumer prices rose 3.3 percent, the highest rate since a 6.1 percent increase in 1990. They had risen 2.5 percent in 1995.
The "core rate" for last year presented a more benign picture. It rose by only 2.6 percent, the smallest rise since an identical increase in 1994. It rose by 3.0 percent in 1995.

The increase in December and for all of 1996 partially reflected a jump in energy prices, the Department said. Energy rose by 1.6 percent in December after being up 1.2 percent in November. For all of 1996, it rose by 8.6 percent, the fastest increase since an 18.1 percent rise in 1990.
Food and beverage prices helped to moderate inflation in December, rising only 0.1 percent after being up 0.3 percent in November.
Transportation costs rose 0.6 percent while medical care increased by 0.2 percent and entertainment by 0.4 percent.
